purpose: Behavioural model of historical Magnus Carlsen move choices. Outputs a distribution over LEGAL moves; not an evaluator of move quality.

tensors.squares: long [B, 64]  piece id per square (0..12), side-to-move frame
tensors.history_from: long [B, 5]  last moves' from-squares, newest first, 64 = pad
tensors.history_to: long [B, 5]  last moves' to-squares, newest first, 64 = pad
tensors.speed: long [B]  time-control class (0..5): unknown, ultrabullet, bullet, blitz, rapid, classical
tensors.ep: long [B]  legal en-passant file 0..7 or 8 = none
tensors.numeric: float [B, 10]  castling x4, halfmove/100, fullmove/100, played_as_black, time_control_present, log base time, log increment

layout.[0, 4096): from_square*64 + to_square (normal moves, castling, en passant, queen promotion)
layout.[4096, 4162): underpromotions: 22 rank7->rank8 pawn (from,to) pairs x {rook, bishop, knight}

output.frame: side-to-move (board mirrored vertically when Black is to move)
output.head: attention-style: score(from,to) = <W_q h_from, W_k h_to>/sqrt(64) + learned 64x64 bias; underpromotion score = pair score + learned per-piece bias

legal_move_masking: logits at illegal indices are replaced by -1e9 before softmax; a row with zero legal moves (mate/stalemate) raises ValueError. Any legal move has a slot, so coverage does not depend on which moves occur in the training data.
